title: Show your cleaning routine in a short video
simple_explanation: A 30-second video of how you clean tools and chairs removes the main fear customers have before visiting.
do_this: Film your staff wiping the chair, swapping towels, and dipping tools in sanitiser before a customer sits.
Add a small caption on the video: 'How we clean before every customer at {{businessName}}.'
Post it on Instagram Reels and also send it as a WhatsApp Status.
Save the video on your phone so you can send it on WhatsApp when someone asks 'Is your place clean?'
copy_ready_text: Hi! Here is how we clean before every customer at {{businessName}} in {{location}}. Fresh towel, sanitised tools, wiped chair. You can watch and decide.
example_for_business: {{businessName}} in {{location}} films a quick clip before opening that shows the chair, towel, and tool cleaning steps. The owner saves the same video for WhatsApp replies about hygiene.
why_this_works: Most salon worries are about hygiene. When you show the cleaning step on camera, the customer feels safe before she even arrives.
how_to_know_it_worked: Ask new visitors where they saw your salon. Mark every time someone says they saw the cleaning video or asked fewer hygiene questions on WhatsApp.

title: Reply fast on WhatsApp with a clear price list
simple_explanation: When customers ask 'How much?', they want a clear answer in one message. A ready price list saves you time and stops the price surprise fear.
do_this: Save a price list on your phone with service name and starting price like {{startingPrice}}.
Open WhatsApp Business and put the list in Catalogue so it is one tap away.
When someone messages asking the price, reply with the catalogue card and one line.
Add a line at the end asking which day they want to come.
copy_ready_text: Hi! Here is our price list for {{serviceName}} starting at {{startingPrice}}. Which day works for you, weekday or weekend?
example_for_business: {{businessName}} in {{location}} sets up a WhatsApp Catalogue with haircut, facial, and threading prices. The owner sends the catalogue card first, then asks which day the customer wants to visit.
why_this_works: Customers decide faster when they see the price in the first reply. A clear list also stops them worrying about extra charges later.
how_to_know_it_worked: At the end of each day, count price chats, catalogue replies, and how many chats have a clear requested day or time.

title: Ask for a Google review right after the service
simple_explanation: A short friendly ask at the right moment helps you collect real Google reviews from customers who already had a good visit.
do_this: Pick a happy customer right after the service ends and before she pays.
Say the review line below and show the Google Maps page on your phone.
Keep a printed card with the Google review link near the billing counter.
Reply to every new review with a short thank you within two days.
copy_ready_text: If you liked the service today, please tap stars and write a few lines on Google. It really helps {{businessName}} in {{location}}. Thank you!
example_for_business: {{businessName}} in {{location}} keeps a small standee at the billing counter with the Google review QR code. After a haircut or facial, the staff gently asks the customer to scan and review before leaving.
why_this_works: New customers often check Google Maps before picking a salon. Real reviews help them feel safer about trying a place they have not visited before.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check Google Business every week. Count how many new reviews were added and whether customers mention the service they used.

title: WhatsApp booking message that confirms time and seat
simple_explanation: When a customer asks for a slot on WhatsApp, reply fast with the time, the service, and the seat. This stops double-bookings and calms the fear of waiting.
do_this: Open WhatsApp Business and keep the chat reply short.
Type the service name, the time slot, and ask 'Shall I fix this for you?'
Save this reply as a quick reply on WhatsApp Business so you can send it in 2 seconds.
Send the salon address pin from your location card after they say yes.
copy_ready_text: Hi {{customerName}}, your {{serviceName}} is fixed for {{timeSlot}} at {{businessName}}, {{location}}. Please come 5 minutes early. Reply YES to confirm. Thank you!
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the owner saves this as a WhatsApp Quick Reply. For each booking, she fills in the service, time, and map pin before sending it.
why_this_works: Customers want a clear yes-or-no answer. A short message with time, service, and place removes confusion and reduces missed appointments.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check confirmed chats at the end of the day. Count how many bookings have a YES reply and a matching appointment entry.

title: Show your patch test and fix-it plan for skin fear
simple_explanation: Many customers worry their skin will react to a new product. A short, clear message about your patch test and safety step calms them before they book.
do_this: Add one line on your WhatsApp catalogue: 'Tell us if you had any skin reaction before.'
Keep your patch-test step written near the billing counter so staff repeat it the same way.
If a customer asks about skin reaction, reply with the message below.
Save the reply as a quick reply on WhatsApp Business.
copy_ready_text: Hi, before we use a new product, we first ask about past skin reactions and do a small patch test if needed. If it does not feel right, we stop and choose a milder option. - {{businessName}}
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the staff saves this as a WhatsApp quick reply. When someone asks 'Will this suit my skin?', they send the reply and explain the patch-test step before booking.
why_this_works: Telling the customer what you will do removes the unknown. A patch test is a small step that shows you care about her skin, not just the service.
how_to_know_it_worked: Track how many chats ask about skin reaction before and after adding this reply. Also note how many first-time customers say the answer made them feel safer.

title: Post a real before-and-after with a clear honest caption
simple_explanation: A real before-and-after photo with a simple honest caption builds trust. No filters, no number claims, just the work and the steps you used.
do_this: Ask the customer if you can share her photo. Only post after she says yes.
Take two photos in the same spot and same light: one before, one after.
Write a caption that lists the service, the steps, and the time taken.
Add your city and your WhatsApp booking line in the caption.
Keep the photo natural, without beauty filters.
copy_ready_text: Before and after at {{businessName}}, {{location}}. Service: {{serviceName}}. Steps: cleanse, trim, shape, finish. Time: {{serviceTime}}. Booking open on WhatsApp. No filters used.
example_for_business: At {{businessName}}, the stylist asks permission, takes the after photo in the same chair and light as the before photo, and posts it with the caption above. No customer name is shown.
why_this_works: Real photos with honest captions beat filtered ads. Local customers can see the work, the time, and the place, so they trust it more.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check the post after two days. Count saves, profile visits, and WhatsApp messages that mention the before-and-after post.

title: Send a simple next-visit reminder on WhatsApp
simple_explanation: A short WhatsApp message after the service tells the customer when to come back. It keeps you in her mind without being pushy.
do_this: After the customer pays, note the next visit date in a small diary or phone note.
Save a reminder message on WhatsApp Business as a quick reply.
Send the message the same evening or the next morning.
Keep it short: service name, date suggestion, and a booking link.
Do not send more than one reminder per visit.
copy_ready_text: Hi, this is {{businessName}}. Your {{serviceName}} is good for the next 3 to 4 weeks. Want me to fix a slot on {{date}}? Reply yes and I will book it.
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the staff writes the next visit date on a small card and saves it in the phone. After the visit is complete, they send the saved WhatsApp reminder once.
why_this_works: Customers forget when to come back. A short note from the salon feels helpful, not salesy, and makes the next visit easier to plan.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check your weekly diary. Count how many next-visit reminders were sent and how many got a reply or confirmed slot.

title: Show your 5 main services in one simple menu
simple_explanation: Customers want to know what you offer and how much it costs before they walk in. A simple menu with your 5 main services removes confusion and stops price questions.
do_this: Pick your 5 most asked services like haircut, facial, waxing, threading, and hair colour.
Write each service name in simple English and your local language.
Add a starting price for each one using {{startingPrice}}.
Print this menu and keep one copy at the billing counter.
Save the same menu as a photo on your phone so you can send it on WhatsApp.
example_for_business: A salon in {{location}} prints this menu and puts it near the entrance. When a new customer walks in and asks 'How much for haircut?', the staff points to the printed menu instead of saying a random price.
why_this_works: A printed menu with clear prices stops the price surprise fear. Customers feel safe when they see the cost before they sit in the chair.
how_to_know_it_worked: Ask staff to mark every price question for one week. Count how many were answered by pointing to the menu instead of guessing prices.

title: Simple first-time visitor offer without fake urgency
simple_explanation: A small, honest offer for first-time visitors helps new customers try your salon without feeling trapped. No countdown timers, no fake hurry.
do_this: Pick one service for the first-time offer, like a basic haircut or simple facial.
Keep the offer open all week, not just for 2 hours.
Write the offer in plain words: what they get, what they save.
Share the offer on your Instagram page and WhatsApp catalogue.
Tell the staff to mention the offer when a new customer walks in or messages.
copy_ready_text: First time at {{businessName}}? Get {{serviceName}} at a special price. No rush, valid all week. Show this message at the counter. - {{location}}
example_for_business: A salon in Kozhikode adds this offer to their Instagram bio and WhatsApp catalogue. The staff saves this line and sends it with the menu when someone asks about prices.
why_this_works: New customers are scared to try a new salon. A small, clear offer lowers that fear and gives them a reason to walk in this week.
how_to_know_it_worked: Ask staff to mark every walk-in or WhatsApp chat that mentions the offer before booking. Review the notes at the end of the week.

title: Add real service photos and service list to Google Business
simple_explanation: When people search 'salon near me' on Google, your photos and service list are the first thing they see. Real photos of your work help them pick you over the next shop.
do_this: Open your Google Business profile on your phone.
Go to the Photos section and upload 8 to 10 real photos of your salon, your staff working, and finished work like haircuts and facials.
Go to the Edit menu and add your 5 main services with starting prices using {{startingPrice}}.
Add your opening hours, phone number, and {{location}} clearly.
Ask 3 regular customers to leave a Google review this week.
copy_ready_text: {{businessName}} in {{location}}. Services: haircut, facial, waxing, threading, hair colour. Walk-in welcome. Book on WhatsApp: [your number]. Open 10am to 8pm.
example_for_business: A salon owner in Kozhikode spends 20 minutes one evening adding real photos of clean chairs, staff working, and finished haircuts to their Google Business page. They also list their 5 main services with starting prices and check the profile from another phone.
why_this_works: Most local salons leave their Google page empty. Adding photos and a service list makes your page look real and active, so new customers trust you before they even visit.
how_to_know_it_worked: Your Google Business profile shows photos and a service list when you search your salon name on Google Maps.

title: Show the consultation step before the service starts
simple_explanation: A short consultation before the service helps the customer feel heard. It shows your stylist listens and plans before starting.
do_this: Before any haircut or colour, ask the customer three questions: what length, what look, and any past hair problem.
Write the answers in a small notepad near the chair.
Show two similar work photos from your phone if you have permission to use them.
Ask one final question: 'Shall I start with this plan?'
Keep the same question list at every chair so staff follow the same process.
copy_ready_text: Before we start, can I ask 3 quick questions? What length do you want? Any hair issue? Do you have a photo of the look you like? I will plan the steps first. - {{businessName}}
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the stylist keeps a small notepad by the chair and writes the customer's length, look, and past hair issue before starting the service.
why_this_works: Most bad-result fear comes from being misunderstood. A two-minute consultation shows the customer that the stylist has listened before touching the hair.
how_to_know_it_worked: Track how many haircut or colour customers finish without asking for changes. Also note how many complaints mention 'not what I asked for'.

title: Send a polite WhatsApp message when the slot is late
simple_explanation: When your chair or stylist is running late, a quick honest WhatsApp message keeps trust. Hiding the delay makes customers more upset.
do_this: Send the message as soon as you know the delay.
Keep it short: sorry, reason, new time, and a choice.
Offer two options: wait for the next chair or shift to a later slot.
Save this as a WhatsApp Business quick reply.
If the delay becomes longer, send one more short update.
copy_ready_text: Hi, sorry. Your slot at {{businessName}} is running about {{delayMinutes}} minutes late. You can wait, or I can shift you to {{newTime}}. Which is better for you?
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, when a colour service takes longer than planned, the front desk sends this saved WhatsApp reply and lets the customer choose whether to wait or shift.
why_this_works: Customers can accept a delay when they know what is happening. A clear update with two choices feels respectful and reduces angry waiting.
how_to_know_it_worked: Count how many late-slot customers still arrive after receiving the message. Also track complaints about waiting time each week.

title: Send simple aftercare steps after the service
simple_explanation: Customers forget what to do at home after a facial, colour, or styling service. A short written note reduces confusion.
do_this: Pick the three services that need aftercare, like hair colour, facial, or styling.
Write three simple aftercare points for each service.
Give the customer the card before payment.
Send the same points on WhatsApp the same evening.
Add one line telling them to message the salon if they feel itching, redness, or hair trouble.
copy_ready_text: After your {{serviceName}} today: 1) Follow the wash timing we told you. 2) Avoid heat, sweat, or harsh products today. 3) Message {{businessName}} if you feel itching, redness, or hair trouble.
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the stylist gives a small aftercare card after hair colour and sends the same points on WhatsApp in the evening.
why_this_works: Written aftercare is easier to remember than verbal advice. It also shows the customer that the salon cares after the bill is paid.
how_to_know_it_worked: Count aftercare questions, repeat calls about what to do, and skin or hair complaints each week.

title: Book a bridal makeup trial the simple way
simple_explanation: A trial visit lets the bride see the look before the wedding day. It also gives time to check style, timing, and skin comfort.
do_this: Set one fixed trial slot per week so you are not rushed.
Ask the bride to bring one or two reference photos on her phone.
Tell her the trial timing clearly before she comes.
Do a small patch test first if she has sensitive skin.
Write down the products used and the look agreed in a notebook.
Send the agreed look summary on WhatsApp after the trial.
copy_ready_text: Hi, this is {{businessName}} in {{location}}. For your bridal trial, please share 1 or 2 reference photos. Trial timing: {{trialTime}}. Patch test can be done if needed. Shall I fix the slot?
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the owner fixes one trial slot, asks for reference photos, notes the products used, and sends the agreed look summary on WhatsApp after the trial.
why_this_works: Brides feel safer when the look is tested before the event. A written summary also prevents confusion between trial day and wedding day.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check that each bridal trial has a notebook entry, reference photos, product notes, and a WhatsApp summary saved before the final event date.

title: Turn a walk-in into a fixed booking for a longer service
simple_explanation: Walk-in customers may ask for long services like colour, smoothening, or bridal prep. A fixed slot protects their time and your chair.
do_this: Ask which service the walk-in customer wants.
Check how much chair and stylist time the service needs.
Offer the next clear slot today or tomorrow.
Write the name, phone number, service, and slot in the appointment diary.
Send a WhatsApp confirmation with date, time, and service name.
Ask the customer to reply YES so the slot is clearly confirmed.
copy_ready_text: Hi {{customerName}}, your slot at {{businessName}} is fixed for {{bookingDate}} at {{bookingTime}} for {{serviceName}}. Please reply YES to confirm. Thank you.
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, when a walk-in asks for hair smoothening, the staff explains the time needed, writes the slot in the diary, and sends the WhatsApp confirmation while the customer is still at the counter.
why_this_works: A clear date and time feels safer than a vague 'come later'. The WhatsApp confirmation also reduces confusion for both staff and customer.
how_to_know_it_worked: At closing time, check whether every long-service walk-in has a diary entry and a matching WhatsApp confirmation message.

title: Send a polite message when a customer misses an appointment
simple_explanation: When a customer misses a slot, a polite message keeps the relationship open and helps you free the chair without sounding angry.
do_this: Wait 15 minutes after the slot time before messaging.
Send one short WhatsApp asking if the customer is still coming.
Wait a little longer for a reply.
If there is no reply, send one reschedule message.
Mark the slot as open in your diary.
Keep the tone soft and helpful, not blaming.
copy_ready_text: Hi {{customerName}}, we waited for your {{serviceName}} slot at {{businessName}}. Hope everything is okay. We have freed this slot. Reply with a new date and time if you want to reschedule.
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the front desk waits 15 minutes, sends the first WhatsApp, then marks the slot open in the diary if there is no reply after the reschedule message.
why_this_works: A calm message protects trust. It also gives the salon a clear rule for freeing the chair instead of waiting without a plan.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check the appointment diary each week. Count missed slots, rescheduled slots, and how often the two-message rule was followed.

title: Simple weekday student offer with clear ID check
simple_explanation: Students want a fair price but may feel shy to ask. A simple weekday offer with a clear ID check makes the offer feel fair and respectful.
do_this: Pick one weekday like Tuesday or Wednesday for the student offer.
Choose one service like basic haircut, simple cleanup, or threading.
Set a clear starting price like {{startingPrice}} for students with a valid college ID.
Save the offer as a WhatsApp quick reply and a small poster at the billing counter.
Train staff to ask for ID politely before confirming the price.
copy_ready_text: Hi! Students with a valid college ID get {{serviceName}} at {{startingPrice}} on weekdays at {{businessName}}, {{location}}. Show your ID at the counter. No rush, book your slot here.
example_for_business: {{businessName}} in {{location}} puts up a small card near the billing counter that says 'Student Offer - show ID, get basic haircut at {{startingPrice}} on Tuesday and Wednesday'. Staff ask for the ID before starting the service. The same line is saved as a WhatsApp quick reply.
why_this_works: Students trust clear prices more than hidden discounts. A weekday offer can support slower days without creating fake urgency.
how_to_know_it_worked: Count how many student offer slots are used on the chosen weekday. Ask staff to mark whether each student came from WhatsApp, Instagram, or walk-in.

title: Mother-daughter family visit plan with set services and timing
simple_explanation: Families often want to visit together but worry about long waits. A simple family plan with services and timing makes the visit easier to understand.
do_this: Pick two services that work well together, like haircut for mom and simple facial for daughter.
Set a fixed family slot on a slow day like a weekday afternoon.
Block two chairs side by side or one chair pair for the family.
Write the package as 'Mom + Daughter' or 'Family of 2' with a starting price like {{startingPrice}}.
Save the package as a WhatsApp quick reply and a small printed card at the counter.
copy_ready_text: Mom and Daughter package at {{businessName}}, {{location}}. Two chairs, one time slot, services: {{serviceName}}. Starting at {{startingPrice}}. Book a weekday slot on WhatsApp.
example_for_business: {{businessName}} keeps a small printed card at the counter: 'Mother-Daughter Plan - haircut for mom, simple cleanup for daughter, two chairs side by side, starting at {{startingPrice}}'. Staff also save the same line as a WhatsApp quick reply and block two chairs for the chosen weekday afternoon.
why_this_works: Family customers feel safer when they know the timing, services, and starting price before they come. A fixed slot also helps the salon avoid overbooking.
how_to_know_it_worked: Count family package bookings each week. Ask staff to mark whether the booking came from WhatsApp, counter, Instagram, or Google Business.

title: Show men grooming hygiene before booking
simple_explanation: Men trying a grooming studio for the first time may worry about hygiene, bad cuts, or unclear prices. A simple card shows the setup before they visit.
do_this: List three main men services like haircut, beard trim, and clean shave with starting price {{startingPrice}}.
Take three photos: clean tools on a tray, fresh towel, and chair cleaning.
Save the photos in WhatsApp Catalogue and Google Business photos.
Write one WhatsApp reply with services, starting prices, and slot timing.
Keep the same three-service card at the counter.
copy_ready_text: Men grooming at {{businessName}}, {{location}}. Haircut, beard trim, clean shave from {{startingPrice}}. Fresh towel and clean tools for every customer. Send your preferred time to book.
example_for_business: {{businessName}} keeps three photos ready in the WhatsApp Catalogue: clean tools, fresh towel, and chair cleaning. The staff uses the same service list on WhatsApp, Instagram, and the counter card.
why_this_works: Clear services, visible cleaning, and a simple booking line remove the first-visit fear. It also keeps the answer consistent across staff.
how_to_know_it_worked: Count men grooming enquiries, booked slots, and which photo or service list was sent in each WhatsApp chat.
